items.title: For a flat map of Noetherian rings the completed Ext agree with the Ext of the reduced modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a flat homomorphism A -> B of Noetherian rings, an ideal I of A, A-modules M and N, and sets B_n = B/I^nB, M_n = M/I^nM, N_n = N/I^nN; assuming M is flat over A it asserts the displayed equality of inverse limits relating the completed Ext^i_B(M, N) to Ext^i_{B_n}(M_n, N_n) for all i (source lines 29370-29385). The proof is an explicit comparison of two complexes computing the two families. It chooses a resolution ... -> P_2 -> P_1 -> P_0 -> M -> 0 by finite free B-modules P_i and sets P_{i,n} = P_i/I^nP_i; flatness of M and B over A makes the reduced sequence ... -> P_{2,n} -> P_{1,n} -> P_{0,n} -> M_n -> 0 exact (proof lines 29388-29396). The proof then observes that the complex Hom_B(P_0, N) -> Hom_B(P_1, N) -> ... computes Ext^i_B(M, N), while the complex Hom_{B_n}(P_{0,n}, N_n) -> Hom_{B_n}(P_{1,n}, N_n) -> ... computes Ext^i_{B_n}(M_n, N_n) (proof lines 29397-29406). The substantive step is the termwise identification Hom_{B_n}(P_{i,n}, N_n) = Hom_B(P_i, N)/I^n Hom_B(P_i, N) (proof lines 29406-29409). Applying the second part of the Artin-Rees consequence to the two complexes gives the asserted equality of limits (proof lines 29410-29411). The non-routine content is the exactness of the reduced resolution, which is what makes the second complex compute the reduced Ext, together with the termwise identification feeding into Artin-Rees.
